name: North Face (Beckey-Schmidtke Route)

waypoints.name: Nooksack Cirque Trailhead (Trail #750)
waypoints.note: Ford Ruth Creek on a log right at the trailhead — no bridge; a crossing that's dry in the morning can be thigh-deep by afternoon in summer.
waypoints.directions: From Bellingham, take Interstate 5 to the Sunset Drive/Mount Baker exit and follow the Mount Baker Highway (WA-542) east through Glacier, the last place to resupply groceries, to the Nooksack River bridge about 13 miles past town. Turn left onto Nooksack River Road (Forest Service Road 32) immediately before the bridge, staying left at 0.5 miles and right at 1.4 miles from the highway. The road washes out at 2.3 miles; park there at Ruth Creek, about 2,156 feet, since the road is not drivable beyond that point. A North Cascades National Park backcountry permit is required for overnight stays: $10 per person plus a $6 reservation fee, reserved on Recreation.gov. In-person pickup is at the Glacier Public Service Center on Thursdays and Fridays in season; a walk-up can be requested by email the morning before.

waypoints.name: Off-trail ford of the Nooksack River
waypoints.note: Leave the Nooksack Cirque Trail here (flagged but easy to miss) and drop steeply to ford the Nooksack before climbing the forested ridge toward Price Lake.
waypoints.directions: Cross Ruth Creek on a log or by wading at the trailhead, then follow the old roadbed about 2 miles to the original Nooksack Cirque trailhead near 2,550 ft. From there, watch for a flagged, easy-to-miss spot where the climbers' route leaves the trail and drops steeply to the Nooksack River.

waypoints.name: Price Lake
waypoints.note: Reliable water at the lake outlet; the boot path climbs the ridge along the lake's north side up onto the moraine above.
waypoints.directions: Ford the Nooksack on a log if one is in place (they are swept away and replaced most years), then climb the steep forested slope toward Price Lake, starting up the west bank of Price Creek until a sound log lets you cross it, and continue to the lake at about 3,900 ft.

waypoints.name: Moraine bivy at ~5,900 ft
waypoints.note: Last reliable flat rock for bivy bags before the tower, with a gentle slope leading directly onto the Price Glacier.
waypoints.directions: From the lake, climb onto the moraine above it and follow the crest of the rib upward on a faint goat path to flat rock slabs at about 5,900 ft, the last good bivy before the tower.

waypoints.name: Price Glacier crossing
waypoints.note: Rope up and cross the crevassed lower Price Glacier toward the tower's base; move fast — the traverse sits under rockfall-prone slopes off the tower's north face.
waypoints.directions: Rope up and get onto the glacier, traverse climber's right to an exposed snow saddle below the tower, then descend from it onto the main lobe of the Price Glacier and cross the crevassed lower glacier toward the tower's base. Losing height off the saddle is correct.

waypoints.name: Steep snow/ice gully
waypoints.note: 50°+ snow/ice gully funnels rockfall from above; climb it early in the day before the sun loosens debris.
waypoints.directions: Cross the bergschrund at about 6,500 ft at the foot of the north face (when it is hollow, parties swing wide left) and climb into the couloir above it on 50-degree snow and ice, early in the day before the sun starts rockfall.

waypoints.name: Nooksack Bivouac saddle
waypoints.note: Flat, often snow-covered col between the tower and the connecting ridge; used as a high bivy and as the rappel-anchor point on the descent.

waypoints.name: Nooksack Tower summit
waypoints.note: Small, exposed summit block with a brass Mountaineers register and loose rock near the top.

approach: From Bellingham, exit Interstate 5 at Sunset Drive/Mount Baker exit. Drive Mount Baker Highway (Washington 542) east through the town of Glacier (last resupply for groceries) and continue 13 miles to the Nooksack River bridge. Immediately before the bridge, turn left on Nooksack River Road (USFS #32). Stay left at 0.5 miles, stay right at 1.4 miles from highway. Continue to the washout at 2.3 miles from the highway and park at Ruth Creek (elevation 2,156 feet). Hike the abandoned road beyond the washout for two miles to the original Nooksack Cirque trailhead at 2,550 feet. River ford the Nooksack (use the log crossing at the original location noted at N48.87097 W121.61267; new logs are often swept away). Proceed up the forested mountainside east of the creek, starting up the west bank of Price Creek until finding a good log crossing. Continue to the moraine above Price Lake (3,911 feet), then hike the ridgeline between Price and East Nooksack Glaciers upward from the moraine to a rock slab bivouac spot at approximately 5,900 feet. From the bivouac, gain the glacier, traverse climber's right along the glacier to an exposed snow saddle below Nooksack Tower, then drop down and work onto the main lobe of the Price Glacier.

approach_variants.name: Ruth Creek washout, Nooksack Cirque, Price Lake moraine and the ridge to the 5,900 ft slab bivy
approach_variants.notes: From the Mount Baker Highway, turn left onto Nooksack River Road (FS-32) immediately before the Nooksack River bridge, about 13 miles past Glacier. Stay left at 0.5 miles, right at 1.4 miles, and park at the washout at 2.3 miles from the highway, by Ruth Creek at about 2,156 ft. Walk the abandoned road beyond the washout for two miles to the original Nooksack Cirque trailhead at 2,550 ft. Ford the Nooksack. There is a recorded log crossing near N48.87097 W121.61267 — new logs get swept away every year, so treat the coordinate as where to start looking rather than as a bridge. Go up the forested mountainside east of the creek, starting on the west bank of Price Creek until a good log turns up. Continue to the moraine above Price Lake at 3,911 ft, then follow the ridgeline between the Price and East Nooksack Glaciers up to a rock slab bivouac around 5,900 ft. From the bivy, get onto the glacier, traverse climber's right to an exposed snow saddle below the Tower, then drop down and work onto the main lobe of the Price Glacier. This route belongs to Nooksack Tower and not to Mount Shuksan — it was merged from a duplicate Shuksan entry, and the Price Glacier route on Shuksan is a different climb sharing much of the same ground.
approach_variants.season: Roughly Jun-Aug. Earlier the river is high and the couloir is safer; later the river drops but the couloir bakes and sheds rock
hazards: Fording the Nooksack on logs that are swept away and replaced yearly
Rockfall down the couloir, recorded on the first ascent and in every account since
A hollow bergschrund that has forced parties to swing wide left
A descent of roughly ten 60 m rappels off gear you build yourself — fixed anchors here should not be trusted
Parties routinely still on the couloir or the lower approach after dark; one team took 21 hours from camp back to camp
approach_variants.baseFinding:
The bergschrund at roughly 6,500 ft is the base, and the couloir above it is the only one. Beckey and Schmidtke's own account of the first ascent puts them at the bergschrund at the foot of the final north face at 6,500 ft, with 800 ft of 50-degree ice couloir above. That is the arrival: a schrund, then a single steep couloir that guards the Tower.

The ridge between the two glaciers is the handrail. From the Price Lake moraine you climb a rib with the Price Glacier on one side and the East Nooksack on the other. In cloud you do not need the Tower: keep a glacier on each side of you and go up. If you only have ice on one side, you have come off the rib.

The saddle is the hinge, and it is counterintuitive. From the bivy the traverse is climber's right to an exposed snow saddle below the Tower, and then you drop down onto the main lobe of the Price Glacier. Losing height here feels wrong and is correct. A party that refuses to descend off the saddle stays high on the wrong side and never reaches the couloir.

Confirm at the schrund: the couloir starts around 50 degrees and steepens to about 60 at the top, with a single 70-degree step where it hits rock. If your line eases off rather than steepens, it is not the couloir. Parties have found the schrund hollow and swung wide left to avoid it entirely — that is a known variation, not a sign you are lost.

What going too far looks like: continuing up the Price Glacier past the Tower's couloir puts you on the Price Glacier route on Shuksan, which is a different mountain's climb reached from the same basin. Nooksack Tower is the freestanding tower below and north of Shuksan's summit; if the ground above your couloir keeps going for thousands of feet rather than ending on a tower in about 1,200 ft of fourth class, you are on Shuksan.
